findings.reason: the node's gate would pass an implementation that silences the hold on a genuinely changed section, which is the failure the section exists to prevent.
findings.text: the first case ("a section edit the write response reports as owing nothing leaves the queued request admissible") is satisfied by any implementation in which admission copies the write response, including one where that response wrongly reports nothing owed; the three negative controls all break the *sharing* of the coverage call, never its correctness, so no arm of this gate can distinguish two readings that agree from two readings that are right

findings.reason: a worker handed no durable log path writes to its scratchpad or records none, and the promotion receipt then carries `test_logs` and `baseline_suite` it cannot fill, so the section's own evidence is unverifiable after the run.
findings.text: s45 (and s44 likewise) says only that "the armed suite command passes at the head, judged by delta against the dispatch base", naming no path for either arm's log, while s37, s39 and s50 each require every log to sit under the run directory and to start with its revision and end in `EXIT=`

findings.reason: each site is also named by its symbol (`_plan_review_record_for_promoting_run`, the verbatim `if committed_review_payloads and not already_promoted` guard, `_WRITE_PATHS_SENTENCE`), so a worker greps to the right line and no node's mechanism turns on the number.
findings.text: `promotion_checks.py:2429-2430` is cited as the `_plan_review_record_for_promoting_run` `None` return, but those lines fall in `_landing_scope_products`; the return the section describes is at line 2637. s39's `promotion.py:1674` and s45's `plan_review.py` "near line 4712/4741" have drifted the same way, to 1886 and 5246/5275

findings.reason: implemented literally, every finding whose anchor is a code path or a line number falls outside the uncovered units and is demoted to an observation, so the gate would lose the in-scope findings it exists to hold on; the section must make the attribution explicit — either require the brief to carry each finding's unit, or state how an unattributable finding is treated.
findings.text: the deliverable splits a re-review's findings into those "on those units" and those "on the other units, which the edit did not change", but a stored finding carries only `anchor`, parsed as the report's free-text `<file>:<line>` token (`_parse_plan_finding` in `reckon/crew/review.py`, the record documented at `parse_plan_review_report`), and the content brief requires no plan unit on a `FINDING` line, so nothing in the record maps a finding to a section and the classification has no defined input

findings.reason: the node can unify the two readings in either direction, and unifying on the write response's file (a worktree checkout, say) makes both quiet on the very edit whose §8 run the hold was right to refuse, so the section's root cause and its done-when point at opposite repairs.
findings.text: the Why cites a write response reporting `review_owed: []`, then a direct call made an hour later to the same predicate, `plan_review.review_coverage`, on the same plan, returning `uncovered = ["s8"]`, and admission agreeing with that later reading; the evidence therefore identifies the write response as the under-reporting reading, yet the deliverable makes admission hold "only on what the write response would report as owed" without stating which reading is repaired, and its own candidate list leaves "the plan file it reads" open

rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — s44 and s45 are the only unimplemented sections whose done-when names no durable path for their gate logs, where s37, s39 and s50 each state that every log sits under the run directory.
